clue.text: Tom's had dining room fight broken up by famous last words

indicators.note: a fight that is broken up is split apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone called Tom has had a scrap in the dining room, and it ends with a memorable parting line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken up' rearranges all twenty-two letters of TOMS HAD DINING ROOM FIGHT. The Two Ronnies was a long-running BBC comedy show starring Ronnie Barker and Ronnie Corbett, and this line closed every episode.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase was the closing line spoken at the end of each episode, so it is literally a well-known final utterance.

clue.text: A very loud man involved in noisy dispute

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud
Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A shouting man gets caught up in a loud quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public brawl or disturbance of the peace, a rowdy quarrel by another name.

clue.text: Book a pair of performers a short time after start of last month

a means one, the Roman numeral I
mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: Someone booking a double act for just after the beginning of December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' reads as a verb meaning to hire, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A duodecimo is a small book size made by folding each sheet into twelve leaves.

clue.text: Teacher, oddly, is a creature with hair reaching the knees

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and seventh, of the word teacher

explanation.definitionFit: The tahr is a Himalayan wild goat whose shaggy coat hangs long, a mane down towards its knees.

explanation.walkthrough: 'cells' looks like prison cells or batteries but means the reproductive kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Gametes are reproductive cells, sperm or eggs, that fuse in fertilisation.

explanation.surface: Someone quarrelling with pupils at an Islamic school somewhere in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of madrasa are A, R, S, placed inside OMAN. 'row' sounds like a quarrel but is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower propels a boat with oars, so one who rows is a person handling the oars.

clue.text: All points supported by actors on TV series in role of either Ronnie at the end of the show

definitions.text: role of either Ronnie at the end of the show

on places the last piece below what comes before in a down answer

parts.note: N, E, W, S are all four compass points
the cast is the company of actors in a production
ER was a long-running American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: Actors on a TV show playing a part, with both Ronnies in some role as the programme ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The Two Ronnies, a classic BBC comedy show, ended with Barker and Corbett sitting at a desk reading spoof news items.
explanation.definitionFit: Both comedians closed each show posing as bulletin readers, reading out comic items like presenters of the news.

explanation.definitionFit: Grebo is slang for a long-haired rock-loving biker or follower of grunge-style music.

clue.text: Part of the furniture — Ronnie obviously wasn't this

Ronnie Corbett was famously short, so he was not a lofty lad

explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie Corbett, the shorter of the Two Ronnies, was barely five feet tall; read the answer as two words for this sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The furniture piece is a tall chest of drawers; split, the letters say a lofty lad, which Corbett was not.

clue.text: See 1
Angrily shouted at slippery customer having heard of poor treatment

explanation.surface: Someone yelled furiously at a shifty character after hearing about bad treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippery customer' suggests a con man but is a literal eel. The match relies on a non-rhotic British accent, where roared drops its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is unfair or harsh treatment, getting the short end of the stick.

clue.text: Summit making primate cross

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing in cash machine' sounds like a sorry tale of no money, but O goes inside ATM.

explanation.definitionFit: Burkina Faso was called by this name until 1984, so it is a former nation in West Africa.

explanation.walkthrough: 'without a stop' looks like nonstop; 'stop' alone is the definition, an organ stop, and 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: On a pipe organ a stop selects a rank of pipes, and the diapason is the main foundation stop.

clue.text: I didn't get that sad

feeling regret or pity, as in feeling bad for someone

clue.text: Killer sent to a prison

explanation.walkthrough: 'without resistance' reads as unopposed, but 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmanned aerial vehicle flown remotely is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Some protection from treaty south of France set up

explanation.definitionFit: A dust cap is a small cover that shields a valve, lens or bearing from dirt, a form of protection.

clue.text: One of the Larkin girls captivating revenueman initially in teatime adaptation

an adaptation reworks material, so the letters of teatime are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of revenueman

explanation.surface: A Larkin daughter charms a taxman during a dramatised teatime scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The Larkins are the family in The Darling Buds of May, a popular British TV adaptation of H. E. Bates's novel; the eldest daughter is the one named here.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest Larkin daughter in the Bates stories bears this name, so she is one of the family's girls.

clue.text: Sea Mist — a creation of a French artist

explanation.surface: Sea Mist sounds like the title of a painting by a French master.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a leading French painter of the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: Malaysian ready to telephone unpleasant chap

explanation.definitionFit: The ringgit is the currency of Malaysia, its ready money.

clue.text: Displaying great relish at the prospect of ITV Anglia's broadcast

clue.text: For every French artist, repeatedly taking in capitals of Nigeria and Ghana, that's always attractive
